title: G1: Derive the geodetic Diophantine system and justify the exact count 5376

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Gap G1 (load-bearing).** The statement asserts geodeticity of the subdivision $G'$ reduces to a system of exactly **5376** linear Diophantine equations/inequalities in the 175 edge-length variables $\{x_e\}$, from the 5-cycles and 6-cycles of $H$.

*Verified numerically* (Robertson pentagon/pentagram model): $|E(H)|=175$, **1260 pentagons**, **5250 hexagons**, 7-regular, triangle-free.

Must PROVE:
(1) For a generic pentagon and hexagon, the explicit arc-length (in)equalities forcing a unique geodesic between each pair of branch vertices (arcs summing to $s_1,s_2$: uniqueness on that pair $\iff s_1\neq s_2$ when the cyclic path is the geodesic; equalities arise where two routes are forced equal).
(2) These local conditions over all 1260 pentagons + 5250 hexagons are jointly NECESSARY for $G'$ geodetic.
(3) Reconcile the bookkeeping to obtain exactly 5376 constraints. Note $1260+5250\neq5376$, so the precise counting/deduplication argument is nontrivial and must be reconstructed.
Downstream gaps G2-G5 depend on this.
